text:
B: Hiya. Can you hear me?
A: Yes, perfectly, thank you. I'm Martin.
B: Gemma. Peterborough. You're the engineer, I think? Claire mentioned.
A: That's me, yes. Structural, mostly historic bridges. And you're in quality, I gather?
B: Quality engineer. Engines and generators. Supplier stuff, root cause when parts fail inspection.
A: Ah, so you're the detective at your end too. That's the bit of my job I like best, working out why something's gone wrong, or in my case why it hasn't.
B: Same. Most people hate it. I quite like sitting a supplier down and just asking for the data until it comes out.
A: Well, er, I suspect you're better at that than I am. I tend to give people the benefit of the doubt for a bit too long.
B: I give them about one meeting, to be fair. Did you do engineering at uni, then?
A: Bristol, a very long time ago. Nineteen eighty-four. What about you?
B: Apprenticeship at sixteen, machining. Then BTEC, HNC on day release, and a part-time BEng in my late twenties. Nights, while working full-time.
A: That's a lot harder than the way I did it, you know. I just turned up at eighteen and somebody else paid.
B: Ha. It was alright. My dad used to tell everyone at the club about it.
A: I'm sure he did. He must have been very proud.
B: He was. He passed four years ago. So, I noticed the books behind you in your photo. Proper reference books.
A: Some of them are older than I am. And I noticed your plastering, actually. Is that your own work?
B: It is. Spare room. Half done. Everyone's mentioned it today, Callum said it was stressing him out.
A: Ha. I'm trying to fix a sash window in our back bedroom at the moment, and it's been about four months, so I'm in no position to judge.
B: Is it the cords?
A: Partly the cords, partly about a hundred years of paint holding it shut. I've got as far as taking the beading off and then sort of stalled.
B: That's the worst bit, to be fair. Once it's open you just crack on.
A: That's what my wife says. What do you do outside work, then?
B: Five-a-side Wednesdays, parkrun Saturdays at Ferry Meadows, the dog. I keep a log of my times. I'm a bit sad about it.
A: Not at all. I've got a sourdough starter I keep notes on, and I'm convinced Helen's feeding it behind my back because it's doing far better than it should.
B: Have you asked her?
A: She denies everything.
B: You need a controlled trial. Mark the jar.
A: That's a genuinely good idea. I'll put a line on it tonight with a pen.
B: Then you'll have data. Do you walk much? You look like you're outdoors a lot.
A: The South Downs, most Saturday mornings. I saw a red kite last weekend over—
